#' Acquire Netflix What We Watched Reports
#' 
#' This function will acquire and standardize all data for MP#01
#' from Netflix. Because Netflix hosts the data files behind a CDN, we
#' are accessing the release pages and automatically extracting links to the
#' relevant files (with CDN hash). 
#' 
#' After import, files are stacked vertically and some basic cleaning is
#' performed. 
load_netflix_data <- function(){
  # Note to students: Make sure you have installed the tidyverse and fs packages
  #                   before beginning this assignment. If you aren't sure,
  #                   simply run `library(tidyverse)` at your R Console and, if
  #                   you don't see an error message, `tidyverse` has been 
  #                   installed. (Same for `fs`) If you still need to install
  #                   either package, use the `install.packages` function as 
  #                   demonstrated in class.
  library(tidyverse)
  library(rvest)
  library(readxl)
  library(fs)
  
  data_dir <- path("data", "mp01")
    
  if(!dir_exists(data_dir)){
    dir_create(data_dir, showWarnings=FALSE, recurse=TRUE)
  }
  
  NETFLIX_URLS <- list(
    `2023H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-a-netflix-engagement-report",
    `2023H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2023",
    `2024H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2024",
    `2024H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2024",
    `2025H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2025",
    `2025H2` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-second-half-of-2025",
    `2026H1` = "https://about.netflix.com/news/what-we-watched-the-first-half-of-2026"
  )
  
  download_if_needed <- function(url, local){
    if(!file_exists(local)){
      download.file(url, local, quiet = TRUE, mode = "wb")
    }
    
    return(local)
  }
    
  NETFLIX_URLS |> 
    map(read_html) |> 
    map(html_element, xpath = "//a[contains(@href, '.xlsx')]") |> 
    map_chr(html_attr, "href") |> 
    enframe("period", "url") |> 
   mutate(path = path(data_dir, paste0(period, ".xlsx")), 
          path = map2(url, path, download_if_needed), 
          data = map(path, read_excel, skip=3, na="*"), 
          data = map(data, \(x) x |> mutate(`Release Date` = as.Date(`Release Date`)))) |>
    unnest(data) |> 
    select(-url, -path) |> 
    mutate(year=str_sub(period, 1, 4), 
           half=str_sub(period, start=6), 
           period_start = make_date(year, if_else(half==1, 1, 7), 1), 
           period_end = make_date(year, if_else(half==1, 7, 12), if_else(half==1, 30, 31))) |> 
    filter(!is.na(`Hours Viewed`)) |> 
    mutate(live_event = !is.na(Runtime) & str_detect(Runtime, "\\d+:\\d+\\*"), 
           clean_time = str_remove(Runtime, fixed("*")),
           Runtime = 60 * hour(hm(clean_time)) + minute(hm(clean_time))) |>
    select(-clean_time) |>
    mutate(Runtime = coalesce(Runtime, mean(Runtime, na.rm=TRUE)), 
           .by=Title, 
           Title = stringi::stri_trans_general(Title, "Latin-ASCII"),
           Title = str_remove(Title, " // .*"), 
           Title = str_remove(Title, "[^[:ascii:]].*"), 
           Title = str_trim(Title)) |>
    filter_out(Title == "") |>
    select(year, 
           period, 
           period_start, 
           period_end, 
           Title, 
           -half, 
           Runtime, 
           Views, 
           `Hours Viewed`, 
           `Release Date`,
           `Available Globally?`, 
           live_event) |>
    # Task 2
    rename(
      title = Title,
      runtime = Runtime,
      views = Views,
      hours_viewed = `Hours Viewed`,
      release_date = `Release Date`,
      available_globally = `Available Globally?`
    ) |>
  # Task 3
    mutate(
      year = as.integer(year),
      available_globally = available_globally == "Yes"
    )
}

NETFLIX_DATA <- load_netflix_data()

Data Acquisition - State Electricity Profiles
The data was acquired from the EIA website that combined all information into one data set on all 50 states, including CO₂ emissions, primary energy sources, electricity prices, and total electricity generation.


Show Code
get_eia_sep <- function(state, abbr) {
  library(tidyverse)
  library(stringr)
  library(httr2)
  library(rvest)

  state_formatted <- str_to_lower(state) |>
    str_replace_all("\\s", "")

  dir_name <- file.path("data", "mp02")
  file_name <- file.path(dir_name, state_formatted)

  dir.create(dir_name, showWarnings = FALSE,
             recursive = TRUE)

  if (!file.exists(file_name)) {
    BASE_URL <- "https://www.eia.gov"

    RESPONSE <- request(BASE_URL) |>
      req_url_path(
        "electricity",
        "state",
        state_formatted
      ) |>
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` =
          "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0"
      ) |>
      req_perform(file_name)

    resp_check_status(RESPONSE)
  }

  TABLE <- read_html(file_name) |>
    html_element("table") |>
    html_table() |>
    mutate(Item = str_to_lower(Item))

  if ("U.S. rank" %in% colnames(TABLE)) {
    TABLE <- TABLE |>
      rename(Rank = `U.S. rank`)
  }

  CO2_MWh <- TABLE |>
    filter(Item == "carbon dioxide (lbs/mwh)") |>
    pull(Value) |>
    str_replace_all(",", "") |>
    as.numeric()

  PRIMARY <- TABLE |>
    filter(Item == "primary energy source") |>
    pull(Rank)

  RATE <- TABLE |>
    filter(Item == "average retail price (cents/kwh)") |>
    pull(Value) |>
    as.numeric()

  GENERATION_MWh <- TABLE |>
    filter(Item == "net generation (megawatthours)") |>
    pull(Value) |>
    str_replace_all(",", "") |>
    as.numeric()

  data.frame(
    CO2_MWh = CO2_MWh,
    primary_source = PRIMARY,
    electricity_price_MWh = RATE * 10,
    generation_MWh = GENERATION_MWh,
    state = state,
    abbreviation = abbr
  )
}

EIA_SEP_REPORT <- map2(
  state.name,
  state.abb,
  get_eia_sep
) |>
  list_rbind()

load_ntd_energy <- function(){
  library(readxl)
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
  

  DATA_DIR <- file.path("data", "mp02")
  dir.create(DATA_DIR, showWarnings=FALSE, recursive=TRUE)

  NTD_ENERGY_FILE <- file.path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_energy.xlsx")

  if(!file.exists(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
  
    request("https://www.transit.dot.gov/sites/fta.dot.gov/files/2026-09/2025%20Energy%20Consumption_260806.xlsx") |>
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)$size < 1e4){
        cat("I was unable to download the NTD Energy File. Please try again.\n")
        stop("Download failed. Please delete corrupted file and try again.")
    }

  to_numeric_fill_0 <- function(x){
    x <- if_else(x == "-", NA, x)
    replace_na(as.numeric(x), 0)
  }

  read_excel(NTD_ENERGY_FILE) |> 
    select(-c(`Reporter Type`, 
              `Reporting Module`, 
              `Gallons of Other Fuel`, 
              `Other Fuel Description`)) |>
    mutate(across(-c(`Agency Name`, 
                     `Mode`,
                     `TOS`), 
                  to_numeric_fill_0)) |>
    group_by(`NTD ID`, `Mode`, `Agency Name`) |>
    summarize(across(where(is.numeric), sum), 
              .groups = "keep") |>
    mutate(ENERGY = sum(c_across(c(where(is.numeric))))) |>
    filter(ENERGY > 0) |>
    select(-ENERGY) |>
    ungroup()
}

NTD_ENERGY <- load_ntd_energy()




Transit Service Data

load_ntd_service <- function() {
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)

  DATA_DIR <- file.path("data", "mp02")
  dir.create(DATA_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

  NTD_SERVICE_FILE <- file.path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_service.csv")

  # Download data only if the file does not exist
  if (!file.exists(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)) {

    request("https://data.transportation.gov/resource/4fir-qbim.csv") |>
      req_url_query(`$query` = paste(
        "SELECT `_5_digit_ntd_id` AS `NTD_ID`",
        "`max_agency` AS `AGENCY`",
        "`max_reporter_type` AS `reporter_type`",
        "`max_organization_type` AS `organization_type`",
        "`max_city` AS `city`",
        "`max_state` AS `state`",
        "`mode`",
        "`type_of_service`",
        "`max_primary_uza_code` as `uza_code`",
        "`max_primary_uza_name` as `uza_name`",
        "`max_primary_uza_area_sq_miles` as `uza_sq_miles`",
        "`max_primary_uza_population` as `uza_population`",
        "`max_service_area_sq_miles` as `service_area_sq_miles`",
        "`max_service_area_population` as `service_area_population`",
        "`questionable_record` as `flagged_likely_inaccurate`",
        "`sum_unlinked_passenger_trips_upt` as `total_upt`",
        "`sum_passenger_miles` WHERE caseless_one_of(`report_year`, '2025') limit 50000",
        sep = ","
      )) |>
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0"
      ) |>
      req_perform(path = NTD_SERVICE_FILE)
  }

  if (file.info(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)$size < 1e4) {
    cat("I was unable to download the NTD Service File. Please try again.\n")
    stop("Download failed. Please delete corrupted file and try again.")
  }

  read_csv(
    NTD_SERVICE_FILE,
    col_types = cols(
      total_upt = col_character(),
      .default = col_guess()
    )
  ) |>
    mutate(
      total_upt = parse_number(total_upt),
      flagged_likely_inaccurate = !is.na(flagged_likely_inaccurate)
    )
}

Show Code
library(tidyverse)


service_data <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  transmute(
    NTD_ID = str_pad(as.character(NTD_ID), 5, pad = "0"),
    Mode = mode,
    state = state
  ) |>
  distinct(NTD_ID, Mode, .keep_all = TRUE)


agency_states <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  transmute(
    NTD_ID = str_pad(as.character(NTD_ID), 5, pad = "0"),
    state = state
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(state)) |>
  distinct() |>
  group_by(NTD_ID) |>
  filter(n_distinct(state) == 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  rename(agency_state = state)


energy_data <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  mutate(
    `NTD ID` = str_pad(as.character(`NTD ID`), 5, pad = "0"),
    Mode = recode(
      Mode,
      "Aerial Tramway" = "AR",
      "Alaska Railroad" = "AR",
      "Bus Rapid Transit" = "RB",
      "Cable Car" = "CC",
      "Commuter Bus" = "CB",
      "Commuter Rail" = "CR",
      "Demand Response" = "DR",
      "Ferryboat" = "FB",
      "Heavy Rail" = "HR",
      "Hybrid Rail" = "YR",
      "Inclined Plane" = "IP",
      "Light Rail" = "LR",
      "Monorail/Automated Guideway" = "MG",
      "Motor Bus" = "MB",
      "Streetcar Rail" = "SR",
      "Trolleybus" = "TB",
      "Vanpool" = "VP"
    )
  )


combined_data <- energy_data |>
  left_join(
    service_data,
    by = c("NTD ID" = "NTD_ID", "Mode" = "Mode")
  ) |>
  left_join(
    agency_states,
    by = c("NTD ID" = "NTD_ID")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    state = coalesce(state, agency_state)
  ) |>
  select(-agency_state) |>
  left_join(
    EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
      select(abbreviation, CO2_MWh),
    by = c("state" = "abbreviation")
  )


combined_data |>
  summarize(
    total_rows = n(),
    missing_states = sum(is.na(state)),
    missing_co2 = sum(is.na(CO2_MWh)),
    duplicate_agency_modes = n() -
      n_distinct(`NTD ID`, Mode)
  )

The combined data including EIA electricity data, NTD energy consumption data, and NTD transit service data, contained 1,134 records of transit agencies and transportation modes.
By calculating the CO2 fuel emissions and electricity usage, we are able to analyze how much CO2 emissions is produced by each transit agency. Using the glimpse function, we are given an overview of the data set’s dimensions, column names, data types, and sample records.


Show Code
emissions_data <- combined_data |>
  mutate(
    
    fuel_emissions_lbs =
      coalesce(`Gallons of Diesel Fuel`, 0) * 22.45 +
      coalesce(`Gallons of Gasoline`, 0) * 20.86 +
      coalesce(`Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas`, 0) * 20.86 +
      coalesce(`Gallons of Liquified Nat Gas`, 0) * 9.75 +
      coalesce(`Gallons of Liquified Petroleum Gas`, 0) * 12.68 +
      coalesce(`Gallons of Bio-Diesel`, 0) * 0 +
      coalesce(`Gallons of Ethanol`, 0) * 0 +
      coalesce(`Kilograms of Hydrogen`, 0) * 0,

    
    electricity_MWh =
      (
        coalesce(`Kilowatt hours of Electric Battery`, 0) +
        coalesce(`Kilowatt hours of Electric Propulsion`, 0)
      ) / 1000,

    
    electricity_emissions_lbs = if_else(
      electricity_MWh == 0,
      0,
      electricity_MWh * CO2_MWh
    ),

    
    total_emissions_lbs =
      fuel_emissions_lbs + electricity_emissions_lbs
  )

glimpse(emissions_data)

Normalize Emissions to Transit Usage
I combined the total CO₂ emissions and total passenger usage data, which will be useful when comparing how much CO₂ each transit agency produces per passenger trip and per passenger mile.


Show Code
agency_emissions <- emissions_data |>
  group_by(`NTD ID`, `Agency Name`) |>
  summarize(
    total_emissions = if (
      all(is.na(total_emissions_lbs))
    ) NA_real_ else sum(total_emissions_lbs, na.rm = TRUE),
    missing_emissions = any(is.na(total_emissions_lbs)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

agency_usage <- NTD_SERVICE_FIXED |>
  mutate(
    NTD_ID = stringr::str_pad(as.character(NTD_ID), 5, pad = "0")
  ) |>
  group_by(NTD_ID) |>
  summarize(
    total_upt = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_passenger_miles = sum(sum_passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

agency_efficiency <- agency_emissions |>
  left_join(
    agency_usage,
    by = c("NTD ID" = "NTD_ID")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    emissions_per_upt = if_else(
      total_upt > 0 & !missing_emissions,
      total_emissions / total_upt,
      NA_real_
    ),
    emissions_per_passenger_mile = if_else(
      total_passenger_miles > 0 & !missing_emissions,
      total_emissions / total_passenger_miles,
      NA_real_
    )
  )

2025 annual “greenest” public transit agency award
Introduction:
The Green Transit Alliance analyzed several public transit agencies and how they performed from an environmental standpoint using the National Transit Database (NTD) and the Energy Information Administration. In this year’s award ceremony, we gave out two awards. The first award recognized the agency with the most pollution for every mile a passenger travels, while the second award recognized the most environmentally friendly transit agency.


Greenest Transit Agency
This award was given based on the calculations in which we divided the total CO₂ emissions by total passenger miles for different public transit agencies and then arranged the agencies from lowest to highest emissions per passenger mile. Based on the results, City of Seattle was the greenest transit agency producing 0.0639 pounds of CO2 per passenger mile. The median agency produced 1.1845 pounds of CO2 per passenger mile.

Memo:
This memo will provide recommendations on ways Netflix can strengthen its strategy for 2027 and beyond. All evidence used to support my recommendations comes from Netflix data from the period 2023H1 to 2026H1. The two topics that I will be addressing are TV shows vs. movies and ‘Big hits’ vs. the long-tail of smaller titles. That being said, when it comes to Netflix producing more movies or TV shows in 2027 and the years after, I think it is important to prioritize investing their money into creating more TV shows rather than movies. When looking at different periods, specifically 2023H2 and 2026H1, the data showed that TV shows made up 95.78% and 94.75% of the total viewing hours. On the other hand, the data showed that movies made up only 3.55% and 3.23% of the total viewing hours. By evaluating these numbers, you can see that there is a major difference in the number of hours viewed between TV shows and movies. Although the data for TV showed a slight decrease, overall we can see that it remained consistently high. This demonstrates that Netflix viewers are spending more of their time watching TV shows rather than movies. Based on this data, Netflix should invest its money in this type of content, as this type of content is what is most watched on their platform.
Another recommendation I have for Netflix is that they should continue to invest in big hit titles, but they should not put all their energy into them and can also invest in smaller titles. I say this because when looking at the top 10 titles, even though their hours viewed are high, it only makes up a very small percentage of the total viewing on Netflix.
